title: Normalized proper/open interchange commutes with projection
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and consider a commutative square of schemes
$$\begin{array}{ccc}A&\xrightarrow{k}&B\\ r\downarrow&&\downarrow p\\ C&\xrightarrow{i}&D\end{array}$$
with $k,i$ quasi-compact open immersions and $r,p$ proper. No Cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites, and put $P_h=Lh^*$ and $R_h=Rh_*$. Put $B_C=B\times_D C$, with projections $b:B_C\to B$, $q:B_C\to C$, and $s=(k,r):A\to B_C$. Use the clopen immersion $s$ and projection $\pi_s:F\to s_!s^{-1}F$ that is identity on $s(A)$ and zero on the complementary open. Let
$$\alpha:P_pi_!\xrightarrow{\beta}b_!P_q\xrightarrow{b_!\pi_sP_q}b_!s_!s^{-1}P_q\cong k_!P_r$$
and let $\gamma:i_!R_r\to R_pk_!$ be its proper-adjunction mate, with precisely the normalization of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Let $\pi_h$ be the counit-defined projection maps of [def-exchange-projection] and $\delta_i,\delta_k$ the canonical open tensor isomorphisms of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. For every derived object $M$ on $A$ and $N$ on $D$,
$$\gamma_{M\otimes^L P_rP_iN}\,i_!(\pi_{r;M,P_iN})\,\delta_i
=R_p(\delta_k)\,\pi_{p;k_!M,N}\,(\gamma_M\otimes 1).$$
Both sides go from $i_!R_rM\otimes^L N$ to $R_pk_!(M\otimes^L P_rP_iN)$, using the canonical pullback identifications. The identity is natural and requires no Tor or boundedness condition on $M,N$.
The same identity holds as an equality before evaluation in the unbounded derived categories of strict semilinear coefficient systems $((A_{E,n})_T)_n$ on the pro-etale sites, with exact system pullbacks, derived system direct images, termwise open extensions, system tensor and the intrinsic system comparison $\Gamma_Q$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. In that version $\alpha$ is the same clopen-projection composite on the ringed diagram sites and $\gamma=\Gamma_Q$. It is an equality of system maps, not a conclusion from their evaluated equalities.
